decisions: THERE ARE THREE MONTH QUESTIONS AND THEY MUST STAY APART. currentMonthKey() - which month is it NOW (lib/utils, local). localMonthKeyOf(iso) - which month did THIS happen in (lib/utils, local). monthKeyOf(iso) - the same, but bucketed by the UTC instant (lib/commission). monthKeyOf is correct by design: UTC is what makes payroll grouping deterministic across machines. The bug was never monthKeyOf itself, it was comparing its output against a LOCAL month key - two sides, two clocks.

THE COLUMN TYPE DECIDES THE HELPER. trips.trip_date and customer_topups.topup_date are DATE columns, already local calendar terms, so a plain slice (monthKeyOf) is correct and they were deliberately left alone. trips.delivered_at is TIMESTAMPTZ and must convert first (localMonthKeyOf). Leaving the DATE sites is a decision, not an oversight.

localMonthKeyOf SHORT-CIRCUITS A BARE YYYY-MM-DD, and that guard is load-bearing. These call sites sit beside DATE-column ones, and new Date('2026-08-01') parses as UTC midnight, so west of Greenwich it shifts back a day and on the 1st back a MONTH. Measured under TZ=America/Los_Angeles: naive gives 2026-07 for '2026-08-01' and 2025-12 for '2026-01-01'; the guard gives 2026-08 and 2026-01. That bug could never have reproduced in Riyadh, which is exactly why it needed a guard rather than a comment.

FIXING HALF A DEFECT FAMILY IS HOW THE OTHER HALF COMES BACK AS A FRESH BUG. The ask named CustomersTab; BreakdownReport carried the identical expression twice, two lines from code being edited anyway, so all four sites moved together.

MONEY CODE WITH NO PRODUCTION CALLER IS LEFT ALONE. lib/commission-rows.ts has two more monthKeyOf(delivered_at) sites, in buildBaseLines (zero callers, ts-prune reports it unused) and buildCommissionRows (called only by its own harness). The live UI uses the rolling API keyed on payout_id IS NULL, not on a month. Changing them is risk without benefit.

A MODULE-LEVEL CONST THAT READS THE CLOCK IS A BUG, NOT A CACHE. The original CURRENT_MONTH_KEY was computed once at module load and never rolled over. The UTC skew was the smaller half. Anything answering 'what is now' must be called, not captured.

MONTH_KEY IS LOAD-BEARING ON THE WRITE PATH. v_commissions_monthly attributes specials, adjustments AND the bonus by exact string match, and v_driver_payslip_basis reads through it. The 'month_key is kept only as a human label' comment on setCommissionBonus describes that upsert's CONFLICT TARGET (driver_id alone), not the views.

THE DIRECTION OF A DEDUPE IS DECIDED BY CONSUMERS. monthKeyOf's surviving copy is the one 4 modules already imported; the copy with 0 external consumers was deleted and proven byte-identical to the survivor first.

THE DATE-HELPER MAP, now final. lib/utils.ts owns the LOCAL clock: todayKey (today, YYYY-MM-DD), daysAgoKey (n days back, same clock; NEGATIVE n goes forward, which is how today+7 is expressed), currentMonthKey (this month, YYYY-MM), localMonthKeyOf (the month of a stored timestamp, converting the instant first, with a bare-date short-circuit). lib/commission.ts owns the UTC BUCKETER: monthKeyOf, the only definition, for grouping stored timestamps into payroll periods deterministically. Five helpers total; do not add a sixth without reading those. SIX THINGS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD. (1) tests/month-keys.spec.ts pins the boundary and runs under four timezones (Riyadh, UTC, Los_Angeles UTC-8, Kiritimati UTC+14). It needs no diagnostic route and no auth bypass, so unlike the older suites it does not rot at teardown. RUN IT IN A NEGATIVE-OFFSET TZ after any date-helper change - the bare-date guard is invisible in Riyadh. (2) Remaining toISOString() uses in app/ and lib/ are TIMESTAMPS (terminated_at, decided_at, updated_at) and are legitimate; only DATE KEYS were ever wrong. (3) NO LIVE FIGURE MOVED in this last fix: of 730 delivered trips, ZERO bucket differently under UTC vs Riyadh today. It closed a latent hole.
